Earlier this year, rumors swirled that a redesigned Health app would debut with iOS 26.4. That effort was subsequently delayed, and even some time after iOS 27's release, the rewritten Health app still hasn't materialized.

With the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 set to launch next month, it's worth exploring whether related new features will be announced at the same event.

Precedent

First, it's worth recapping why these features are very likely to be announced in September. You might think, "Shouldn't all software be released in June?" — but there is indeed precedent for this.

Features like watchOS 9's Low Power Mode, watchOS 11's sleep apnea detection, and watchOS 26's hypertension notifications don't actually require the latest hardware to function, yet all were only officially announced in September.

Therefore, based on the above reasons, Apple is very likely to wait until September to unveil the latest Health app upgrades, even if these features don't necessarily require a brand-new Apple Watch to use.

There's Still Time

Ahead of WWDC27, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman warned that the Health app upgrade, codenamed "Project Mulberry," might not make an appearance at the WWDC keynote. As it turned out, he was right:

Does this mean Project Mulberry will definitely appear at the September event? Not necessarily. However, given that features have been announced in September before, and we already know the project may launch later than WWDC, the chances of a September debut look pretty high — though it may ultimately have to wait until October, arriving alongside iOS 27.1.

Feature Recap

With so many factors involved, rumors have been flying thick and fast. You may have heard about a standalone Health+ service, complete with videos shot by doctors. However, according to reports, those plans have been scaled back, and the functionality will instead be integrated into the existing Health app experience.

That said, two things are already quite clear: first, an AI health coach will be introduced to provide health advice based on your Health app data; and second, real-time guidance for workouts and other health-related tasks will be available via the camera. Another key highlight of this upgrade is that the Health app will feature a brand-new design, making it easier for users to understand their data.

Beyond that, we'll just have to wait and see. Personally, I'm really looking forward to having a better way to organize and understand my Apple Health data.
